verses.text: Yahweh appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.
He lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw that three men stood opposite him. When he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,
and said, “My lord, if now I have found favor in your sight, please don’t go away from your servant.
Now let a little water be fetched, wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
I will get a morsel of bread so you can refresh your heart. After that you may go your way, now that you have come to your servant.” They said, “Very well, do as you have said.”
Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said, “Quickly prepare three seahs  of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.”
Abraham ran to the herd, and fetched a tender and good calf, and gave it to the servant. He hurried to dress it.
He took butter, milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them. He stood by them under the tree, and they ate.
They asked him, “Where is Sarah, your wife?” He said, “See, in the tent.”
He said, “I will certainly return to you at about this time next year; and behold, Sarah your wife will have a son.” Sarah heard in the tent door, which was behind him.
Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age. Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”
Yahweh said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Will I really bear a child, yet I am old?’
Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes round, and Sarah will have a son.”
Then Sarah denied it, saying, “I didn’t laugh,” for she was afraid. He said, “No, but you did laugh.”
The men rose up from there, and looked toward Sodom. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
Yahweh said, “Will I hide from Abraham what I do,
since Abraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed in him?

For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of Yahweh, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that Yahweh may bring on Abraham that which he has spoken of him.”
Yahweh said, “Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous,
I will go down now, and see whether their deeds are as bad as the reports which have come to me. If not, I will know.”
The men turned from there, and went toward Sodom, but Abraham stood yet before Yahweh.
Abraham came near, and said, “Will you consume the righteous with the wicked?
What if there are fifty righteous within the city? Will you consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous who are in it?

Be it far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”
Yahweh said, “If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
Abraham answered, “See now, I have taken it on myself to speak to the Lord, although I am dust and ashes.
What if there will lack five of the fifty righteous? Will you destroy all the city for lack of five?” He said, “I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”
He spoke to him yet again, and said, “What if there are forty found there?” He said, “I will not do it for the forty’s sake.”
He said, “Oh don’t let the Lord be angry, and I will speak. What if there are thirty found there?” He said, “I will not do it if I find thirty there.”
He said, “See now, I have taken it on myself to speak to the Lord. What if there are twenty found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it for the twenty’s sake.”
He said, “Oh don’t let the Lord be angry, and I will speak just once more. What if ten are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it for the ten’s sake.”
Yahweh went his way, as soon as he had finished communing with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.

footnotes.content: I love that the LORD appeared right where Abraham was sitting in the heat of the day. The oaks of Mamre had become a familiar place of meeting with God, and He still draws near to us in the ordinary moments of our lives, pointing us to Jesus who comes to meet us where we are.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham lifted up his eyes and ran to meet three strangers. How much like our Lord, who in His humility came to us as a stranger in love to rescue us. May our hearts learn to run toward others the way Abraham ran toward these men.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham calls them 'My lord' and begs them not to pass by. Little does he know he is speaking to Yahweh Himself. I find such comfort in this: long before we recognized Him, Jesus was drawing near to us and calling us His own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Washing feet was a humble act of hospitality in Abraham's day, not a menial afterthought. Our Savior stooped lower still to wash the feet of His disciples, and ultimately to wash us clean from all our sins by His own blood. What grace that the Master became our Servant!
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham calls it 'a morsel of bread' while preparing a feast for his guests. That is the heart of faith - to give what little we have, trusting that the God who provides will be the one truly serving us. I have learned He always gives far more than we could ever offer Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham hurries Sarah to prepare fine meal for their guests. In a home where the Lord has visited, there is joy and haste to serve. How different from our sluggish hearts, yet how gracious that Jesus Himself hurries to bring us into the joy of His salvation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham runs again - to the herd, to fetch a tender calf. Old age had not made him sluggish in love. I pray the Lord would renew such zeal in this old heart of mine to serve Him and others, especially when I know it is Christ I am serving.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham stands by while they eat, content to serve rather than be served. What a beautiful picture of Jesus, who girded Himself with a towel to serve His people. One day we will feast with Him, but for now He delights to serve us with His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The visitors ask after Sarah by name. The God who called Abraham by name now takes care to ask for Sarah. He knows each of His children personally, and Jesus calls His sheep by name, leading them to green pastures and home to Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The promise comes again: 'I will certainly return to you... and Sarah your wife will have a son.' God is not stingy with His promises. How much more certain are all His promises to us in Jesus, our greater Isaac, through whom every blessing comes to His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham and Sarah were old - well past the point where man would say it was possible. But the God who spoke the world into being delights to show His power in our weakness. He still brings life where there seemed to be only barrenness, ultimately giving us new life in Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sarah laughed within herself at the thought of pleasure in her old age. I understand that laugh - half unbelief, half wonder. The Lord gently deals with our doubting hearts, for He knows we are but dust. Yet He still keeps every word He has spoken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh lovingly confronts Sarah's laughter. He is not harsh with those who tremble, but He will not let us forget the truth of who He is. Our God hears even the thoughts of our hearts, and still invites us to trust Him because nothing is too hard for Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Is anything too hard for Yahweh?' I have asked this question in dark times and have always come back to the same answer - No. If He can raise up Isaac from Sarah's womb, how much more has He raised up our Lord Jesus from the grave for our salvation!
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sarah denied it out of fear, but the Lord gently says, 'No, but you did laugh.' Our God is both tender and truthful with His people. He knows our fears and failures better than we do, yet still covers us with mercy in Jesus, our faithful Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham walks with the men toward Sodom to see them on their way. He shows genuine care for these visitors even as judgment draws near. I am grateful that Jesus walked this earth with us, drawing near to sinners, to seek and to save those who were on their way to judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh asks if He should hide His plans from Abraham. What intimacy! The God who knows all things delights to share His purposes with those He calls His friend. Through faith in Jesus, we too are brought near as friends of God and told of all the Father has given to the Son.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the nations of the earth would be blessed in Abraham. I see now how this pointed to Jesus, the true Seed of Abraham, through whom blessing flows to people from every tribe and tongue. What mercy that we, who were far off, have been brought into that blessing by faith alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God chose Abraham so that he would teach his household to keep the way of Yahweh - to do righteousness and justice. Our great God first chose us in Jesus, and now He teaches us by His Spirit to walk in the righteousness that belongs to us in Christ alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah had reached heaven. Sin does not go unnoticed by our holy God. Yet I take heart - the greater cry of our sin reached the cross, where Jesus bore the full weight of judgment for all His people so that mercy might reign through righteousness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh says He will go down to see. This is condescension beyond measure - the Judge of all the earth comes down to investigate. Our Savior left heaven and came down to earth not to condemn, but to save, taking our place so we might be brought up to be with Him forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The men go toward Sodom, but Abraham remains standing before Yahweh. There is a place of boldness before God for those who know Him. Through Jesus, our great High Priest, we may draw near to the throne of grace with confidence to find mercy in our time of need.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham draws near and intercedes - 'Will you consume the righteous with the wicked?' I see a glimpse of Jesus here, our true Intercessor who ever lives to pray for His people. Because of Him, not one of the righteous - those clothed in His righteousness - will perish with the wicked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham pleads for the sake of fifty righteous. What tenderness for the city! Our Lord loves His elect so much that He pleads for them constantly. He spared not Himself for us, and for the sake of His righteousness alone He has spared all who belong to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?' Abraham knows God's character. I rest in this too - our God is always just. And the wonder of wonders is that at the cross, His justice and mercy met perfectly, as Jesus, the Righteous One, took the judgment we deserved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: For the sake of the righteous, God would spare the whole place. Oh, what a picture of our salvation! For the sake of Jesus, the truly Righteous One, God has spared His whole people - not the city of stone, but a multitude no one can number from every nation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham humbles himself - 'I am dust and ashes.' How right he is. Yet through faith he speaks boldly to the Lord. Even so, we who are dust and ashes may speak boldly to our God only because Jesus, our dust-covered Brother, has made us righteous and brought us near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham persists in prayer, not demanding but pleading. God is pleased to hear such humble intercession. I am learning that the Lord delights for His children to come to Him again and again through Christ, for He has already said 'yes' to us in His beloved Son.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again Abraham speaks up for mercy. The Lord does not grow weary of a praying heart that appeals to His character. How much more should we pray, knowing our prayers are heard for Jesus' sake, who is always praying for us with a love that never fails.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham asks the Lord not to be angry as he continues to plead. I feel the same fear and boldness in prayer. But for those in Christ, there is no anger left for us - all of it was poured out on Jesus. Now only mercy and grace remain for us through Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham takes it upon himself to speak again, still full of humility. Prayer is not twisting God's arm, but leaning into the arms of a faithful God. We can lean hard into those arms because they were stretched out on a cross to embrace us and bring us home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: For the sake of ten, the Lord would spare the city. It was not ten to be found - yet for the sake of the One true Righteous Man, Jesus, God has spared a countless host. May we never tire of marveling at such free and undeserved mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As I look back over a long life of prayer, I see how often the Lord has heard me for Jesus' sake when I had no other hope. Readers today hear an echo of that faithfulness - our great Intercessor still stands before the Father for His people, and He will bring every one of them safely home. As of 2026-10, I am grateful beyond words for such a Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
